newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Japan 96/97 wool buying seen rising - WOOLTEL.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Japan 96/97 wool buying seen rising - WOOLTEL.

text.p: Japan's global purchases of raw wool in the 1996/97 season ending June 30 might rise by 22 percent to 830,000 bales or 121 million kg greasy, international wool intelligence newsletter WOOLTEL said.
The possible rise is attributed to a five percent increase in wool consumption, small stock replenishment and renewal of exports of scoured wool and tops to offshore subsidiaries.
In August this year, the greasy equivalent of total stocks held in Japan had fallen to an historically low level of 22.8 million kg, it said.

WOOLTEL director Lionel Ward said Japan's global purchases in the July-September quarter totalled 143,100 bales, 41 percent up on 1995/96, but still 36 percent below the first quarter of 1994/95, a relatively buoyant season.
Cautious spinning activity was delaying recovery in the important European region, he also said. There had been no flow of improved orders to raw wool markets.
Receding and unstable wool prices in September and October had also resulted in spinners being caught with expensive stock.
